Intercompany eliminations are the accounting adjustments used to remove transactions between entities under the same corporate group during the consolidation process.
These entries ensure the consolidated financial statements reflect only transactions with external parties, presenting a true picture of the group's financial position.
For example, if Subsidiary A sells goods to Subsidiary B for $100, both entities might record that amount as revenue and expense, respectively.
Without elimination, the consolidated revenue would be overstated by $100. By removing this internal transaction, finance teams prevent double-counting and produce accurate, compliant reports.

While the concept is straightforward, execution is not. The more entities, currencies, and ERP systems involved, the more time-consuming and risky the process becomes. What starts as a routine accounting adjustment can easily become a bottleneck for the entire finance function.
